requirements.note: Plain list of all 160 recipes. Each row shows the title, the category (tinted), a clock and the time, a star and the rating, and a chevron. Favorited rows show a small heart.

A scrolling row of chips (All plus all nine categories) stays pinned under the search field. The search matches titles and ingredients and combines with the category: Soups + 'garlic' gives the same 6 results as B. The empty result is a ContentUnavailable-style screen naming the query, with a 'Search All Categories' button.
A Sort menu in the toolbar offers Name A to Z, Time quickest first and Rating highest first, each with an icon and a checkmark. All three work, and the choice survives a relaunch.

The detail screen shows the category, title, rating, total time, a native stepper for servings, bulleted ingredients and numbered steps in circle badges. Stepping works, the minimum is 1 and the minus button greys out there. But scaled amounts mix decimals and fractions ('0.57 cup oil', '⅛ tsp cumin', '0.29 cloves ginger'), which reads badly for a recipe.

A heart in the detail toolbar adds and removes the recipe. A full swipe right on a list row also favorites it. The Favorites tab shows a count subtitle and has a swipe-left 'Remove' action. The empty state reads 'No Favorites Yet' with useful text and a Browse Recipes button.

bugs: Scaled ingredient amounts switch between decimals and fractions in the same list ('0.43 g chickpeas' next to '⅛ tsp cumin'), and some are odd amounts like '0.29 cloves ginger'.
tells: While searching, there is an empty band between the pinned search field and the category chips.
Custom orange accent with chip-style category filters; tasteful, but the chips are hand-built rather than a system control.
The detail screen puts a large hand-laid title in the content with no navigation title until you scroll (acceptable, but unlike a standard large-title push).
A.scroll: The long list scrolls smoothly when dragged slowly and when flung, with no blank or popping rows. It keeps its position after a push and pop and rubber-bands normally at the top. The search field and chips stay pinned.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped list of all 160 recipes. Each row shows the title, 'Category · time', a star and the rating, and a chevron. A header line reads 'All Recipes · 160 recipes · by name'.

A filter menu in the toolbar lists All plus all nine categories with a checkmark. The search field ('Title or ingredient') matches titles and ingredients and combines with the category (Soups + 'garlic' gives 6). The empty result is a 'No Recipes' screen with a Show All Recipes button.
A sort menu offers Name, Time and Rating. All three work, the header shows the current sort, and the choice survives a relaunch.

The detail screen shows the title, category and rating, the time, a native stepper for servings, 'Ingredients for N' with amounts in their own column, and numbered steps. Scaled amounts are tidy fractions (½, 1¾, ⅛). The minimum is 1 and the minus button disables there.

A heart in the detail toolbar adds and removes the recipe. The Favorites tab lists saved recipes with a 'Swipe left to remove' hint and a working Delete action. The empty state reads 'No Favorites Yet' with useful text and a Browse Recipes button.

bugs: A horizontal swipe on a row in the main list opens the recipe instead of doing nothing or showing swipe actions.
tells: The main list has no swipe actions, so you cannot favorite from the list.
Category filtering is hidden in a toolbar menu with no visible chip or scope bar, so it is less discoverable.
The detail screen repeats the title: it appears in the inline navigation bar and again as a bold header in the first card.
Empty-state titles are regular weight rather than the bold of ContentUnavailableView, and the Browse/Show All buttons are untinted grey.
The quantity column on the detail screen is very wide, leaving a large gap before each ingredient name.
The Favorites delete action looks unusual: a round button with a 'Delete' caption underneath and a greyed, rounded row.
The search keyboard opens with Shift on (auto-capitalized).
B.scroll: The list scrolls smoothly when dragged slowly and when flung, with no blank or late-loading rows. It keeps its position after a push and pop and rubber-bands at the top. The search field collapses into the nav bar as standard.

why: Both meet the whole spec and handle dark mode and the largest text size well. A feels more like a finished iPhone app: categories are one tap away in visible chips, there are swipe actions in both lists, and favorited rows show a heart. B's main list has no swipe actions, its filter is hidden in a menu, and its detail screen repeats the title. B's clean fraction scaling beats A's mix of decimals and fractions, but that is not enough to outweigh A's advantages.
